emerging_technology: Agentic AI: software systems that can pursue a bounded goal by selecting and carrying out multiple steps with limited ongoing human direction, while remaining subject to configured controls and escalation. This is the technology category for this case; it does not mean AI generally.
intended_application: Bounded customer-service resolution in e-commerce: an Agentic AI system handles routine delivery-status inquiries and may issue a refund or replacement only within explicit policy and value limits; it escalates exceptions, ambiguous requests, and out-of-policy cases to a human.
organization: Hypothetical e-commerce retailer C, whose leadership is evaluating a broad claim about technology diffusion.
business_need: Leadership wants to know whether current diffusion evidence supports the claim that Agentic AI for retail customer-service resolution has moved into mainstream adoption and whether this should affect the organization's sense of timing.
users_stakeholders: Customer-service agents and supervisors, customers, the operations and technology teams, and executives accountable for service quality and cost.
adoption_posture: The organization has not provided enough case evidence to classify its adopter posture. Do not infer that it is an innovator, early adopter, fast follower, or conservative adopter from the diffusion claim itself.
capabilities_constraints: No organization-specific technical capabilities, deployment history, integration capacity, or adoption behavior are supplied. Treat these as unknown rather than filling gaps with assumptions.
risk_consequence_context: A broad diffusion claim could create false urgency if it is treated as evidence about autonomous agents or retail customer-service resolution. Conversely, broad survey evidence alone cannot establish that the application is rare. The case supplies no organization-specific risk controls or readiness evidence.
management_question: Does the cited evidence support the claim that Agentic AI for e-commerce customer-service resolution has reached mainstream diffusion, and what confidence or timing implication is justified? Identify what more specific evidence would be needed; do not make an adoption decision or design a rollout plan.
time_horizon: Assess the currency and scope of available evidence for the present and near term, up to 12 months.
additional_context: Claim to assess, not a verified conclusion: 'U.S. Census data showed that around 14% of Retail Trade businesses used AI, so around 14% of e-commerce retailers have adopted Agentic AI for customer-service resolution and the application is reaching a mainstream adopter stage.' Source: U.S. Census Bureau, 'Large Firms With at Least 20 Employees Biggest AI Users,' published May 26, 2026: https://www.census.gov/library/stories/2026/05/ai-use-businesses.html. The source reports that in the BTOS period ending May 3, 2026 around 14% of Retail Trade businesses used AI and around 17% expected to use AI in the next six months. BTOS is a biweekly nationally representative survey of U.S. businesses; the measure asks about AI use in any business function over the prior two weeks and expected use over the next six months. Its population is Retail Trade businesses across U.S. geographies, not specifically e-commerce firms; technology is AI broadly, not Agentic AI; applications are any business function, not customer-service resolution; measure is recent self-reported use/intended use, not agentic production deployments or continued use. Therefore these numbers cannot estimate the specified technology/application adoption rate or assign a Rogers stage. Preserve the survey result as broad context, reject the leap, and identify the missing evidence. Do not invent statistics.
